items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: And Henny, I called him Henny, his name was Henry. He played in the district, the red light district.

ctx.x: Never forget music. I love music. My father gave me a trumpet when I was 10 years of age. He went off and came back that afternoon and I played America for him. On the trumpet. I don't know, I must have had a natural ambiture. Because right now I can just get about eight notes out of my horn and I can't practice here. And I'm not going to run to the shrine just because anyone. I have other things to do, things that I would like to do. But I would love to play my trumpet again. But if I couldn't play it the way I…
Did they put a spotlight on you?

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: And Henning died early in life. He was a great trombonist.

ctx.x: And Henning died early in life. He was a great trombonist. And Merrick played a trombone, Abby was a fine trombone, very good one. But he didn't have solidity. You know what I mean? He played in the races and he finally did union moves. But he's a swell guy. He got me up, he pulled me up on a stand on the block in front of a lot of people and he gave me my life's history and all that, and how it made you play.
